chunks: Al-Qasim and ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

When Saʿd died, seventy thousand angels accompanied his funeral procession, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood at his grave and said, ‘Would the likes of Saʿd face the squeezing [of the grave]?’ His mother said, ‘Congratulations to you O Saʿd, and [what a great] honor!’ So the Messenger of Allah said to her, ‘O mother of Saʿd, do not impose anything upon Allah.’ She said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we have heard you say what you said about Saʿd [and how you praised him].’ So he said, ‘Verily Saʿd was harsh in his speech with his family.’

key_terms.أُمُّ سَعْدٍ: Mother of Sa'd, who responded to the Prophet's question.
key_terms.سَعْدٌ: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, a prominent companion of the Prophet.
key_terms.غَلُظٌ: Harshness, roughness, or severity in speech or manner.
key_terms.يَضُمُّ: To squeeze or compress, referring to the punishment of the grave (Dhamm al-Qabr).

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) question if Sa'd would face the squeezing of the grave despite his high status?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Shia scholarly nuance in evaluating Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, distinguishing between his general piety and specific spiritual deficiencies. The Prophet’s (SAW) query, 'Will Sa'd be gathered [in Paradise]?', coupled with the mention of 70,000 angels, underscores the tension between his high rank and the potential for *Barzakh* chastisement due to his *ghilz* (harshness) toward his family. This serves as a practical lesson that even prominent companions are subject to scrutiny regarding their interpersonal conduct, particularly within the domestic sphere.
